FORWARD PLANNING 
 
Variation 3 to the City & County Development Plan 2021 
This Variation seeks to rezone a small portion of green space in Loughboy to residential for 
the purpose of a small number of Age Friendly and Disability Accessible houses. The 
proposed variation along with associated environmental documents were on public display 
for a 6 week period until Friday, 17th January, 2025. A total of 15 submissions were received. 
A Chief Executive’s Report will be brought forward for consideration by the Members at 
the February Plenary Council Meeting. 
 
Variation No. 4 to the City & County Development Plan 2021 
This Variation seeks to incorporate the Loughmacask Masterplan into the City and County 
Development Plan. It also seeks to amend text of Section 10.1.7 of the City and County 
Development Plan, Volume 1 to allow for wastewater treatment plans in certain 
circumstances. This Variation will be on public display for a four week period from Friday, 
7th February to Friday, 7th March, 2025. After this period, a Chief Executive’s Report will be 
prepared and brought forward for consideration by the Members at the March Plenary 
Council Meeting. 
MASTERPLANS 
 
Ballyragget/Paulstown/Kilmacow 
All three Masterplans are now approved by the relevant Municipal Districts. Work has 
commenced to give formal recognition to the Masterplans in the City & County 
Development Plan through a variation, identifying appropriate objectives from all above 
Plans, the Urlingford Masterplan to be implemented and the role of the Masterplans in the 
Development Management process. This to be brought forward in Q1 of 2025. 
LOCAL AREA PLANS 
 
Ferrybank / Belview Local Area Plan 
The Draft Plan preparation continues. Significant issues relating to the role of Ferrybank as 
the second largest Urban Area in the County, its role as part of the wider Metropolitan area 
and its role in contributing to the development of Waterford as envisaged under the 
National Planning Framework, are being addressed as part of the Plan preparation. It is 
anticipated that a Draft Plan will be available in Q1 of 2025.

4 
 
Castlecomer Plan Review Process 
The Plan preparation process continues, with ongoing collaboration between the 
Community and Planning Sections. The Director’s Report on the pre-draft consultation 
stage was published on the Consult website. This outlined the engagement to-date on the 
Plan. The Town Centre Health Check was produced by the Town Regeneration Office in 
January. The Draft Settlement Plan will be accompanied by various assessments, including 
an Infrastructural Assessment and Environmental Assessments. Public display of the Plan 
will take place in Q1 2025.

Active Land Management 
The new Residential Zoned Land Tax (RZLT) comes into effect from February. Two sets of 
maps have now been published for public display, the Final Maps for 2025 and the Annual 
Draft Maps for 2026. Submissions are invited until 1st April. For the Annual Draft Maps, 
submissions can be made on the inclusion or exclusion of sites from scope for the tax. 
Rezoning requests can be made by landowners for impacted sites on the Final Maps 2025. 
The Council prepare the maps, and Revenue will administer the tax. The settlements 
currently liable are Kilkenny City, Rosbercon, Callan and Thomastown. 
There are 18 Vacant Sites on the Vacant Sites Register, and the number of cancelled entries 
due to site activation or improvement is 29. The Vacant Site levy (VSL) will be replaced by 
the RZLT later this year and any outstanding VSL’s will remain due to the Council. 
Conservation 
The Conservation Office manages all protected structures in Kilkenny County and City. 
These structures are recognised for the following special interest: Architectural, Historical, 
Archaeological, Artistic, Cultural, Scientific, Technical, Social. 
An advisory service on conservation matters is provided to the public and colleagues, while 
the conservation grants and funding applications are also delivered. 
Built Heritage Investment Scheme 2025: Extra funding of €54,451 has been acquired by the 
Conservation Office for this scheme, therefore another four projects, which were on the 
Reserve List, have been offered funding. This brings the total funding for Kilkenny Built 
Heritage Investment Scheme to €253,062. 
Historic Structures Fund and the Historic Thatch Building 2025: The deadline for this 
scheme has closed, and applications are now being reviewed. 
Architectural Conservation Area Trails 2024: This project is nearing completion and will be 
launched once final sign off has been undertaken with the National Built Heritage Services 
and Kilkenny’s Architectural Conservation Officer. 
Built Heritage Stocktake 2024: A consultant was appointed to work with Kilkenny County 
Council’s conservation officer and the National Built Heritage Service to deliver a stocktake 
for the following settlements: Callan, Gowran, Inistioge, Johnstown, Thomastown. The 
stocktake will focus on the structures listed on the RPS and NIAH.

ENVIRONMENTAL AWARENESS 
 
Agriculture Map Alerter 
A new Agricultural Map Alerter has been set up on Kilkenny County Council Alerts portal. 
The purpose of the alert system is to notify registered farmers. An active campaign to 
encourage registrations is currently being undertaken.

8 
 
The map of Kilkenny is broken down into Townlands and Electoral Divisions (DEDs) with 
run off times for the spreading of slurry broken into two categories of 48 hours or 96 hours. 
If a Level Yellow/Orange/Red rainfall warning is issued for County Kilkenny then it will 
trigger an SMS message to agricultural alert subscribers, an SMS will go out to the farmer 
highlighting the pollution impact and notifying them not to spread slurry for a period of 48 
hours or 96 hours. 
A basic SMS template is used with a similar image to the one in Wexford County Council 
which breaks down the areas.

Green Schools Programme 
The Environmental Awareness Officer [EAO] continues to support 92 schools as part of the 
An Taisce Green Schools Programme to renew or attain a flag. Green Schools is an 
International Environmental Education Programme, offering a well-defined, controllable 
way for schools to take environmental issues into the curriculum and apply them to the day- 
to-day running of the school. 
 
Green schools is a holistic, long-term programme and has a two-year cycle in relation to 
preparation, assessment and attainment of a particular flag. 
The EAO is continuing to assist schools around the County to renew their membership as 
part of the Green Schools Programme under their respective themes: 
 
▪ Litter and Waste, 
▪ Energy, 
▪ Water 
▪ Travel, 
▪ Biodiversity 
▪ Global Citizenship. 
The EAO will be undertaking assessments of Green Schools over the next 3 months. 
Deadline for the applications for School Flags is 28th March, 2024.

Picker Pals Programme 2024/2025 
 
 
 
The Picker Pals Programme has been designed to deliver deep and sustained behavioural 
change for the primary participants while also affecting peers, family and the broader 
community. We believe no other Environmental Stewardship Programme can provide the 
same depth of benefits. 
Behavioural change is supported by six key pillars: 
1. 
Multimodal Learning 
2. 
Real World, Action-based Learning 
3. 
Boosting Engagement through Responsibility 
4. 
Fun - The Ultimate Motivator! 
5. 
Embedding Behaviour through Personalised Storytelling 
6. 
Community and the Positive Feedback Loop. 
 
In the 2024-25 school year, 32 classrooms from 27 schools are taking part. 
WASTE 
 
Bring Banks Usage 
The Council provides and manages 47 Bring Centers across the City and County. A total of 
2045 tonnes of recyclables were collected from our Bring Centers to date in 2024. This 
represents a 1% increase from the same period in 2023. Loughboy Shopping Centre (20 
tonnes collected), Aldi - Kilkenny City (16 tonnes collected), Lidl – Johnswell and New Park 
Shopping Center, Kilkenny City (12 tonnes collected) are the busiest locations in the City. Lidl 
- Thomastown (11 tonnes collected), Aldi - Ferrybank (10 tonnes collected), and 
Graiguenamanagh and Supervalu - Thomastown (9 tonnes collected) are the busiest outside 
of the City. Environment staff are continuing to work very closely with our service 
providers to ensure the collection service is in keeping with demand, especially around long 
weekends and holiday periods.

PARKS & SPECIAL PROJECTS 
 
The Museum of Medieval Kilkenny 
On the 10th January, 2025, Kilkenny County Council, in partnership with Fáilte Ireland, 
signed a major contract with local company Duggan Lynch Ltd., for the development of 
Kilkenny’s newest tourism attraction. Following an investment of €4.5 million from Fáilte 
Ireland the realisation of this exciting project will enhance the cultural and historical offering 
of the City, attracting more visitors, both national and international, boosting the local 
economy. The “Museum of Medieval Kilkenny” will see a total investment of €8 million 
and provides for the unification of The Tholsel and the Medieval Mile Museum (formerly St. 
Mary’s Church). The overall objective of this project is to develop an offering that will 
become one of Ireland’s top visitor attractions. 
The focus of this current contract will centre on The Tholsel building and includes internal 
and external enhancement works along with the introduction of a lift for improved 
accessibility. These works will safeguard the building into the future and when complete it 
will also continue to act as the seat of Local Government in the City.

Storm Éowyn 
In advance of the Status Red Wind Warning across the entire Country, which came into 
effect in the early hours of Friday 24th January, 2025, in the interest of public safety a number 
of local authority amenities were closed to the public. These amenities included the 
Kilkenny Countryside Park, Silaire Woods and Woodstock Gardens and Arboretum.

14 
 
Unfortunately, a number of trees were damaged and or lost as a consequence of the storm 
in both Silaire Wood and Woodstock Gardens, this was significant particularly in 
Woodstock given the number of important trees already lost during Storm Darragh in 
December last. 
 
 
The Parks Department, once restrictions had lifted, undertook a full assessment of the 
damage and the amenities were reopened to the public once it was considered safe to do so. 
Clean up works were completed in Silaire Woods late last month and a comprehensive 
clean-up will take place in Woodstock Gardens in March, when ground conditions are more 
favourable for the removal of large trees. 
Tree Surgery Works and Hedge Cutting 
Due to recent storms our Tree Surgery Programme was delayed, however, intervention 
works were completed recently in Paulstown, Callan, and Fiddown. Additionally, 
hedgerow maintenance was also completed along the opened section of the South East 
Greenway along with a significant reduction to the beech hedge at Newpark Soccer Pitch. 
Pruning of overgrown trees around the viewing platform on Windgap Hill in the City was 
also completed opening up, once again, fantastic views of Kilkenny Castle.

Broadband/ Digital Update 
County Kilkenny is the second ranked County in Ireland progressing strongly in the 
National Broadband Plan (NBP) roll out at 98% of its intervention area (County Westmeath is 
ranked first with 99%). County Kilkenny has 18,656 premises in its intervention area. 
Currently National Broadband Ireland (NBI) have passed 18,268 or 98% of those premises. 
Of those premises passed, 6,791 or 37% has taken up a NBP connection. NBP proposed an 
investment of €72m for County Kilkenny. The current investment make to date is €70.5m. 
The remaining NBP roll-out will be completed in the coming months with the completion 
of fibre infrastructure works across the County. NBI provide information about the work 
they are doing via their web site, http://www.nbi.ie

The Affordable Homes are generally targeted at first-time buyers (exceptions apply) who 
need assistance bridging the gap between their own available funds (including the Help to 
Buy Scheme), the mortgage that they can obtain and the cost of the new home. Under the 
Affordable Purchase Scheme eligible buyers will be able to purchase their own new home 
by availing of this Shared Equity Scheme. Kilkenny County Council will retain an equity 
share and successful applicants have the option of buying out this share over time. Equity 
shares are calculated on an individual basis and are linked to an applicant’s income, their 
savings and their mortgage capacity. 
 
Under the Affordable Purchase Scheme successful applicants will be able to avail of a

The Tenant (Incremental) Purchase Scheme 2016, which allows Local Authority tenants to 
buy their homes is being revised as of from 29th January, 2024. Changes to the Scheme are 
as follows: 
▪ Minimum Income Requirements: The minimum income required for an applicant to be 
eligible to apply under the scheme has been revised from €12,500 to €11,000 per annum. 
(At least 50% of which must come from a reckonable primary source of income). 
▪ Primary Sources of Income: In addition to employment and the State Pension 
(Contributory and Non-Contributory) being considered as primary sources of income, the 
Widow’s, Widower’s, Surviving Civil Partner’s (Contributory and Non-Contributory 
Pension), Blind Pension, Invalidity Pension and Disability Allowance are now also 
considered primary sources of income. 
▪ Time receiving Social Housing Supports: The period of time tenants will be required to 
be in receipt of social housing support to be considered eligible under the scheme 
remains at 10 consecutive years. However, in the case of joint tenancies only one tenant 
is now required to have been in receipt of social housing supports for 10 years.

The existence of a professional Fire & Rescue Sservice is fundamental to public and personal 
safety. The Fire Service plays a crucial role in making our communities safer, whether it be 
preventing and protecting people from fire and other risks or responding swiftly and 
effectively to the incidents and emergencies that occur 24 hrs per day/7 days per week/365 
days per year. These incidents included a number of road traffic collisions, house fires, 
ambulance assists, public road hazards, car fires, chimney fires and automatic fire alarm 
activations.

on the 24th January, 2025 during Storm Eowyn. They attended fallen Trees in conjunction 
with the Area Offices, Automatic Fire Alarms, structural damage to properties and making

Recruitment of Retained Firefighters 
Our second recruitment campaign is well underway to recruit Fire Fighters in Castlecomer, 
Freshford, Urlingford, Thomastown and Graiguenamanagh. Interviews have been carried 
out. All new recruits will undergo extensive initial training to equip them with the skills to 
be a Retained Firefighter. As well as responding to emergency calls and undertaking 
community fire safety initiatives, Retained Firefighters attend weekly training nights to 
maintain competency levels and undertake routine checks on their equipment. 
 
Retained Firefighters are on call to respond to a range of emergencies. Many Retained 
Firefighters have other full or part-time jobs but when the call comes they are ready to drop 
whatever they are doing and become part of a team, ready to face any emergency. Although 
part-time, Retained Firefighters are fully trained and capable of saving life and property. 
Training 
Kilkenny County Council’s Fire and Rescue Service are obliged under the Fire Services Acts 
1981 and 2003 and the Safety, Health and Welfare at Work Act 2005 to ensure that our Fire 
Fighters and Officers are adequately trained and competent to deal with tasks and varying 
roles they may encounter in the performance of their duties. 
 
All personnel responding to Fire and Rescue Service incidents require a minimum level of 
training to meet core requirements. In addition, many personnel also require further 
training for specialist or supervisory roles. Furthermore, a number of Fire and Rescue 
Service personnel have completed Instructor courses in order that they in turn can instruct 
and direct delivery of training sessions/courses. Personnel also require appropriate 
refresher training in all of the above throughout their careers, generally delivered either 
through on-station training or through specific refresher courses. 
 
 
A number of Fire Fighters and instructors attended a Compartment Fire Behaviour Training 
Course in Hackettstown Fire Training Centre. The aim of this 5 day course is to provide the 
learners (trainee Firefighters), who have completed the 10 day Using Breathing Apparatus 
(Initial Wearer) course, with the skills, knowledge and competency necessary to wear 
Breathing Apparatus in compartment fires. This course provides practical training on the 
knowledge and skills that are required to enable recruit Firefighters to safely work as BA 
wearers at operational incidents, within the incident command structure and BA procedural 
norms.

Hospital to assist staff welfare during the storm. 
The volunteers have responded to several missing person searches in January, including an 
extensive search of the City that went into the early hours of the morning in difficult 
conditions. The volunteers were commended by local Gardai for their incredible responses 
each time. 
The volunteer instructors met early in the month to assist with the development of a training 
plan for the volunteers to ensure upskilling across all areas and the maintenance of their 
incredible standard of training. 
 
With 113 taskings completed in 2024 and 30 taskings completed during the month of 
January, it is shaping up to be another busy year for Kilkenny Civil Defence.

Rates Invoices 2025 
At our Annual Budget Meeting 2025 a Commercial Rates increase of 4% was approved. This 
is only the second time Commercial Rates have been increased since 2008. The prompt 
payment discount was increased to 8.3% (capped at €300 per rate account) from 5.8%. The 
increase in the Prompt Payment Incentive for commercial rate payers would mean that the 
net increase would be less than 2% for the majority of rate payers if they avail of the prompt 
payment discount. Rates Invoices totalling €24.4 million will issue in February to over 2850 
customers.
